questions.explanation: Ellipsis lets us drop the repeated verb: 'but I can't (swim)'.
questions.q: She can swim, but I ___.

questions.explanation: 'Ones' substitutes for the repeated plural noun 'shoes'.
questions.q: I bought the red shoes and the blue ___.

questions.explanation: 'So' substitutes for the whole clause: 'I think so'.
options: Will it rain? I think it.
Will it rain? I think so.
Will it rain? I so think.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: Ellipsis drops the repeated verb: 'than he does (sing)'.
questions.q: She sings better than he ___.

questions.explanation: 'Not' substitutes for the negative clause: 'I hope not'.
questions.q: Is he coming? I hope ___.

questions.explanation: 'One' substitutes for the singular noun 'plan'.
questions.q: The first plan failed; the second ___ succeeded.

questions.explanation: 'Do so' substitutes for the whole verb phrase 'apologize'.
questions.q: You should apologize, but he refuses to ___.

questions.explanation: Ellipsis drops the repeated participle: 'but she has (seen it)'.
questions.q: I haven't seen the new film, but she ___.

questions.explanation: 'Ones' substitutes for the plural noun 'apples'.
questions.q: These apples are fresh; those ___ are not.

questions.explanation: Short answers use ellipsis: 'Yes, I do' (not 'Yes, I like').
options: Do you like it? Yes, I like.
Do you like it? Yes, I do like.
Do you like it? Yes, I do.
Do you like it? Yes, I am.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'So + auxiliary + subject' agrees with a positive statement: 'so does his sister'.
questions.q: He works hard, and so ___ his sister.

questions.explanation: 'Neither + auxiliary + subject' agrees with a negative: 'neither did he'.
questions.q: She didn't come, and neither ___.

questions.explanation: Ellipsis drops the repeated infinitive: 'they said they would (attend)'.
questions.q: Will they attend? They said they ___.

questions.explanation: 'One' substitutes for the singular noun 'a coffee'.
questions.q: I'd like a coffee, and she'd like ___ too.

questions.explanation: Ellipsis drops the infinitive after 'accept': 'we didn't accept (the invitation)'.
options: She can drive, and so can he.
He left early, and she did too.
They invited us, but we didn't accept to.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Others' (= other people) avoids repeating the noun.
questions.q: Some people like tea; ___ prefer coffee.

questions.explanation: Ellipsis drops the repeated participle: 'he says he has (finished)'.
questions.q: Has he finished? He says he ___.

questions.explanation: 'Neither + auxiliary + subject' with singular agreement: 'neither does my brother'.
questions.q: I don't want to go, and neither ___ my brother.

questions.explanation: 'Either' (not 'neither') ends a negative agreement clause: 'she doesn't either'.
options: I don't like it, and neither she does.
I don't like it, and neither does she like.
I don't like it, and she also doesn't.
I don't like it, and she doesn't either.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: Ellipsis drops the repeated verb: 'the board didn't (approve it)'.
questions.q: The manager approved it, but the board ___.
